facts.statement: Bactrosaurus was a herbivorous hadrosauroid dinosaur that lived in Asia between 96 and 85 million years ago.
facts.quote: Bactrosaurus (; meaning "Club lizard," "baktron" = club + sauros = lizard) is a genus of herbivorous hadrosauroid dinosaur that lived in Asia during the Late Cretaceous, from about 96 to 85 million years ago.

facts.statement: The first remains of Bactrosaurus were partial skeletons of six individuals found in the Iren Dabasu Formation of the Gobi Desert, China.
facts.quote: The first Bactrosaurus remains recovered from the Iren Dabasu Formation in the Gobi Desert of China were composed of partial skeletons of six individual B. johnsoni.

facts.statement: Charles W. Gilmore described and named Bactrosaurus in 1933, referencing the large club-shaped neural spines on its vertebrae.
facts.quote: The fossils were described in 1933 by Charles W. Gilmore, who named the new animal Bactrosaurus, or "club lizard", in reference to the large club-shaped neural spines projecting from some of the vertebrae.

facts.statement: A typical Bactrosaurus measured between 6 and 6.5 meters in length and weighed approximately 1.2 metric tons.
facts.quote: A typical Bactrosaurus would have been 6 - 6.5 m long and weighed 1.2 MT.

facts.statement: The femur of Bactrosaurus measured 80 centimeters in length.
Recent studies suggest Bactrosaurus was likely crestless because basal hadrosauromorphs do not preserve hollow crests.
facts.quote: Basal members do not preserve hollow crests, so Bactrosaurus itself is likely to be crestless.

facts.statement: While over 10,000 fossils were examined for tumors, the specific types of tumors found in Bactrosaurus were limited to this genus and closely related genera.
facts.quote: Although more than 10,000 fossils were examined in this manner, the tumors were limited to Bactrosaurus and closely related genera.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the tumors found in Bactrosaurus may have been caused by either environmental factors or genetic propensity.
facts.quote: The tumors may have been caused by environmental factors or genetic propensity.

facts.statement: A 2026 study of fossils collected in 2014 and 2015 suggests Bactrosaurus johnsoni exhibited herding behavior and population segregation between juveniles and adults.
facts.quote: Ma et al. (2026) study the taphonomy and age profile of the assemblage dominated by specimens of Bactrosaurus johnsoni from the Upper Cretaceous Iren Dabasu Formation (China) collected during fieldwork conducted in 2014 and 2015, report that the assemblage is dominated by nestling and juvenile individuals (interpreted as consistent with population segregation between juveniles and adults and with herding behavior of B. johnsoni), and interpret the studied fossil assemblage as likely affected by an attritional mortality pattern.

facts.statement: Bactrosaurus was approximately 6 meters long, 2 meters tall on all fours, and weighed between 1,100 and 1,500 kilograms.
facts.quote: Bactrosaurus medía aproximadamente 6 m de longitud y 2 m de altura sobre sus cuatro patas, con un peso estimado de 1.100 y 1.500 kg soportados sobre un fémur de 80 centímetros.

facts.statement: Bactrosaurus had large vertebral spines that may have supported a hump.
facts.quote: Presentaba grandes espinas vertebrales, las cuales podría haber sostenido una giba.

facts.statement: Like other hadrosaurs, Bactrosaurus could adapt to both bipedal and quadrupedal postures.
facts.quote: Al igual que otros hadrosáuridos, el Bactrosaurus pudo adaptar posturas bípedas y cuadrúpedas.

facts.statement: A subsequent study revealed fragments that appear to be the base of an incompletely preserved crest on Bactrosaurus.
facts.quote: Sin embargo, un estudio, subsiguiente de Bactrosaurus posee piezas al descubierto de lo que parecen ser la base de una cresta de forma incompleta conservada.

facts.statement: Bactrosaurus is classified within the suborder Iguanodontia and the superfamily Hadrosauroidea.
The time range for Bactrosaurus is recorded as extending from the Turonian to the Campanian stages, between 93.9 and 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Turonian to Campanian (93.9 to 72.2 million years ago)

rejected.quote: It shows a number of iguanodont-like features, including three stacked teeth for each visible tooth, small maxillary teeth, and an unusually powerful build for a hadrosaur.
